Nxeon VPS hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`). Real brand tokens live in `app/globals.css` — `--color-brand-500: #6f47f5` (violet), `--color-accent-blue: #3b82f6`, `--color-navy-950: #060a14` through `--color-navy-600`, `--color-accent-cyan: #22d3ee`. Site-wide type is Geist Sans/Geist Mono (`next/font/google`, loaded in `app/layout.tsx`).

## This is a precise implementation task, not creative direction

The owner gave an exact reference mockup image and said: **"stop relying solely on nxeon present assets and styling... but we still want it to still look like nxeon... make it look just like this mockup, everything."** Read that instruction correctly: don't reuse the old template's specific worn-out asset choices (icons, card treatment, the old dotted-map-with-thin-arcs look) — but the color system/typography IS Nxeon's real brand (the reference mockup itself uses blue→violet gradients on navy, which matches the real tokens above exactly) — stay in that palette, just execute it at much higher polish and specificity than what's shipped before. This is your third attempt at this page's hero across this project's history; the first two missed by either being too close to the old template or by abandoning the brand entirely. This reference removes the ambiguity — implement it precisely.

**Scope: hero section ONLY this round.** The owner wants to review this one section before any other part of the page is touched — do not build pricing/FAQ/other sections.

## Exact reference spec (read as a literal implementation spec, not inspiration)

**Left column:**
- A pill badge: small circular Singapore flag icon on the left, "SINGAPORE VPS HOSTING" in caps, small green status dot on the right edge, dark background, thin border.
- Headline: "Singapore VPS" in bold white on one line (very large, ~64-72px), "Hosting" on the next line filled with a blue→violet gradient (left-to-right, `--color-accent-blue` → `--color-brand-500`).
- Sub-copy: "High-performance NVMe VPS hosting from our Singapore datacenter. Built for low-latency connections across Southeast Asia, India, Australia and East Asia." — muted gray, ~2 lines.
- Two buttons: "Deploy now →" (blue→violet gradient fill, arrow icon), "View pricing" (outlined, dark).
- A row of 5 small feature bullets, each a small circular checkmark icon (blue outline) + white text: "Full root access", "NVMe + ZFS", "Dedicated IPv4", "DDoS protection", "Instant deployment".

**Right column — the two elements that matter most, build these with real care:**

1. **Live server spec card** (floats over/beside the map, top-right): dark rounded card, bordered. Header row: small Singapore flag + "sgp1 · Singapore" + a green "● Live" pill on the right. Spec list below: icon + label (gray) + value (white, right-aligned) rows for vCPU (2 vCPU), Memory (4 GB RAM), Storage (50 GB NVMe), Bandwidth (2 TB), IPv4 (Dedicated), Uptime (99.9%) — each row's icon in the blue/violet accent color. Below a divider inside the same card: "Your server is live" with a small elapsed-time badge ("47s") on the right, a horizontal progress bar filled with the blue→violet gradient sitting near 100%, a "100%" label, and an "SSH ready" status line. **This progress bar needs real motion**: animate it filling from 0→100% with a subtle shimmer/sheen moving across the fill, not a static bar — this is explicitly one of the two "most important" pieces to nail.

2. **The grid-map with data-transmission motion graphic — THE most important element in this whole task.** Background: dark navy with a faint technical grid pattern (thin lines) plus a scattered faint particle/dot field — a "digital map" feel, not a literal geographic silhouette. A central glowing Singapore node (bright white/blue dot with a soft pulsing glow halo), labeled with a small flag + "Singapore" in a dark pill. Surrounding it, smaller glowing city nodes each with a label pill showing city name + real-feeling latency in ms: Thailand 20ms, Japan 52ms, India 38ms, Vietnam 22ms, Malaysia 18ms, Indonesia 28ms, Australia 48ms — positioned in roughly correct relative geographic direction from Singapore (Thailand/Vietnam/Malaysia/Indonesia nearby, India northwest, Japan far northeast, Australia southeast). **Curved glowing gradient trail lines (blue→violet) connect the Singapore node outward to every city node, and these must show genuine continuous motion** — a bright pulse or particle traveling repeatedly along each curve from Singapore outward (or an animated dash-offset making each line look like it's actively "flowing" data outward), not static lines. This is the literal "Singapore sending data to surrounding countries" visual the owner called out by name as the thing to dial in. Build this with SVG paths + CSS animation (stroke-dashoffset looping, or an animated marker/dot following each path via CSS motion-path or an SVG `<animateMotion>`) — whatever produces the smoothest, most convincing "live data transmission" effect. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (freeze the animation, keep the static glow/lines visible).

Real numbers: pull the actual live plan spec (2 vCPU/4GB/50GB NVMe/2TB/etc.) from wherever the current Singapore page's plan data comes from (check `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx` and whatever plans/pricing source it reads — a prior audit found the OLD page had a stale hardcoded price; verify against the live DB, don't hardcode a guessed number). Latency figures are presentational/illustrative here (matching the reference's realistic-but-illustrative ms values) — fine to keep them as reasonable static display values unless a real live latency-check mechanism already exists elsewhere in the codebase you can cheaply reuse.

## Technical setup

Two prior full-page attempts at this page exist in git history (branches `feature/singapore-redesign` through `-v4`, all already deleted/rejected) — don't look for or build on any of them, this is a clean restart scoped to just the hero.

`cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-sghero -b feature/singapore-hero-v5`, symlink `.env`, real `node_modules` via `npm ci` (check `df -h /` first, need 5GB+ free). The current `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx` still renders the original shared `<UseCaseLanding>` template — for this round, build the new hero as its own component and swap just the hero portion of that page to use it (leave everything below the hero as whatever's fastest — either keep rendering the rest of the old template content below, or cut the page short; only the hero needs to be complete and reviewable this round). Don't touch `UseCaseLanding.tsx` or the other ~12 pages using it.

`npm run build` + `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Screenshot the hero at 1440px and 390px using Playwright (or whatever's available) — actually look at your own screenshot and compare it section-by-element against this spec before calling it done; if the motion can't be captured in a static screenshot, describe what you built precisely enough that a static frame still demonstrates the animation is real and present (e.g. screenshot mid-animation, or note the exact CSS/SVG technique used so it can be verified by reading the code). Delete your worktree's `node_modules`/`.next` once committed.

Do not merge to main, do not touch staging/production. Commit on `feature/singapore-hero-v5` and stop.

Report back: screenshot paths, the exact animation technique used for the map trail lines and the progress bar (so it can be verified as real motion, not just described), commit hash, confirmation of disk cleanup.
